title: Staying After Graduation: Residence Pathways in Four Countries
seoTitle: After Study: Residence Routes in Four Countries
seoDescription: Compare post-study residence planning in Canada, Australia, Germany and the UK while separating temporary permission from permanent status.
intro: Graduating does not automatically give you permanent residence. Plan around the current route from student status to employment or another eligible status, then check the conditions for longer-term residence.
description:
Graduating does not automatically give you permanent residence. Plan around the current route from student status to employment or another eligible status, then check the conditions for longer-term residence.

A degree is not a residence guarantee

Separate three decisions: where you want to study, what permission you may have after graduation and how you might qualify for longer-term residence. A university admission offer answers only the first of those questions. The immigration route depends on the rules and your circumstances when you apply.

Canada

Check whether your programme and institution meet the current post-graduation work permit requirements. Later permanent-residence routes have their own conditions and selection processes. A Canadian qualification or work permit does not by itself guarantee selection through an economic immigration programme.

Australia

A Temporary Graduate visa and a skilled migration route are different permissions. Eligibility can depend on qualifications, personal circumstances and other conditions. If a later route involves an occupation assessment, nomination or invitation, investigate those requirements separately rather than assuming the degree completes them.

Germany

Check the available route after your studies and the conditions for moving into qualifying work. Longer-term residence depends on the relevant permit and requirements, which can include employment and other evidence. Use the official Make it in Germany guidance and the responsible authority's instructions for your situation.

United Kingdom

The Graduate route provides temporary permission where eligibility conditions are met. It is not itself a guarantee of settlement or future sponsorship. A later work route has separate requirements. Also read any scholarship conditions that require you to leave the UK after the award.

Build a plan you can update

  • Find the official student and post-study route pages for your circumstances.
  • Check the work conditions and the timing for each application.
  • Research realistic jobs for your field, including employer sponsorship where relevant.
  • Record the requirements of the longer-term route separately.
  • Revisit the plan before graduation and before changing immigration status.

Choose a course you can afford and that makes academic and professional sense even if a particular residence route changes. For an individual immigration decision, obtain advice from the relevant authority or an appropriately qualified adviser. A broad comparison cannot determine a person's eligibility.

Ask what the next status would require

A useful residence plan starts with the next eligible status, not a promise of permanent residence. If employment is part of the route, check the job, salary or qualification conditions relevant to that permission. Also check how student time is treated and whether other requirements apply. Record uncertain points as questions for official guidance or a qualified adviser. Rules can change during a multi-year degree, so review the plan at important stages rather than treating today’s requirements as a guarantee of your position at graduation.

Draw the route as a sequence of separate decisions

Start with the permission to study, then identify any temporary post-study route, a possible work or other residence category, and finally the permanent status you are considering. Each transition has its own conditions. Completing a degree may create an option to apply, but it is not the same as meeting every condition of the later route.

Avoid adding the durations of these stages and calling the result a guaranteed settlement timeline. A job offer, occupation requirement, language test, residence period or selection system may affect the next step. The relevant rules can also differ between graduates of different qualifications or institutions. Use the official authority's guidance for your circumstances rather than a single country-ranking graphic.

Questions to verify in each destination

DestinationFirst official checkPlanning question
CanadaPGWP eligibility and relevant permanent-residence programmesWould your programme and later work experience meet the route's conditions?
AustraliaSubclass 485 stream and relevant permanent visaWhich qualification, age, occupation and other conditions apply?
GermanyGraduate job-search and work-residence guidanceWhat qualified employment and residence requirements would the later route need?
United KingdomGraduate route and any subsequent eligible work routeWould the next job and sponsorship arrangement meet the applicable rules?

This table is a research checklist, not immigration advice for a particular person. Use it to decide which official page to read next. Where your history or family circumstances complicate the route, seek advice from an appropriately qualified adviser rather than inferring an answer from another applicant's experience.

Put employment assumptions beside the residence plan

A route requiring qualified employment depends on more than having a degree. Consider how your field recruits, whether professional registration applies, the working language and whether you could realistically meet employer requirements. Research vacancies to understand the market, but do not treat an attractive vacancy today as a job reserved for your graduation year.

If moving with family, examine their permissions separately. The main applicant's right to study or work does not automatically establish every dependant's conditions. Budget using the permissions and costs that are actually confirmed. Do not assume that future employment will resolve a present funding shortfall.

Keep a dated planning record

Write down the official route name, eligibility page, date checked and unresolved questions. Revisit that record before committing to a course, before changing status and before submitting any residence application. This makes it easier to recognise a rule change without rewriting your plans from a social-media headline.

Which country guarantees permanent residence after study?

Do not plan on a guarantee. A degree can be relevant to some routes, but permanent status depends on the applicable conditions and an individual decision.

Should I choose a course only for a residence pathway?

Consider the pathway as one constraint alongside academic value, affordability and employment preparation. A course should remain useful even if the later route or your personal plans change.

Official sources and further reading

Requirements and policies should be checked for your programme and application date. Sources checked on 19 October 2026.

  • GOV.UK: Graduate visa
  • US DHS: F-1 practical training overview
  • Canada: post-graduation work permit eligibility
  • Australia: Temporary Graduate visa, Post-Higher Education Work stream
  • German government: prospects after graduation

Related guides

  • UK, Germany or the Netherlands for a PhD: A Practical Comparison
  • Post-Study Work Options: UK Graduate Visa, US OPT and Other Routes
  • Studying in Germany: Tuition Fees, Living Costs and Funding
